It's a bit of a fallacy to think that an increase in the minimum wage would necessarily (and certainly not proportionally, though you only said considerably, which could be widely interpreted) increase the costs of goods and services. Businesses are not involved in profit maintenance, they are profit-maximizers. You would have to conclude that an increase in the minimum wage would increase the amount of money people were willing to pay for goods and services, or the amounts of them they would want to purchase (it would have to increase demand). This would happen, but people would be doing lots of other things with that new income (medical expenses they couldn't afford before, debt repayment, housing improvements, better education for their children, the list of things people wish they could buy that aren't goods or services in the traditional sense is long).

An increase in demand would create some jobs, too. All of that new demand that would drive up prices somewhat also require more production and service jobs. It's true some businesses running near the red line already might be shuttered, but they are only surviving by depriving their workers of a living wage in the first place, they deserve to fail if they won't cut CEO compensation, or find some other way to stay afloat (in my opinion).
